The clinical presentation and imaging findings are consistent with Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma (PCNSL), and the pathological tests confirm the presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid and a brain biopsy.
Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma is a distinct entity that primarily affects the blood vessels, and the clinical presentation and imaging findings do not support this diagnosis.
Secondary CNS involvement by systemic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma would typically be associated with a known history of systemic lymphoma, which is not mentioned in the case.
Lymphomatosis cerebri variant of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a subtype of PCNSL, but the case does not provide specific information to support this diagnosis over PCNSL.
